scenarios.question: How much did we really grow, once you strip out inflation?

queries.question: Monthly revenue, gross and net of discounts, 2024 and 2025
Consumer price index by month, 2024 and 2025
Gross margin by month and share of units sold on discount

answer.title: Nominal growth vs. real growth
answer.lead: Revenue grew 19.4% year over year, but once you strip out inflation the business shrank 2.5%.

alert.title: Alert: discounting is eating the growth
alert.body: The share of units sold on discount went from 28% to 41%. That jump explains almost the entire margin drop: without it, gross margin would have closed at 40.6%.

answer.conclusion: Bottom line: volume grew, but it was bought with price. The growth showing on the revenue dashboard never reached the result.
answer.followUp: Want me to break the effect down by category, to see where discounting did drive incremental volume?

scenarios.recommendation: Stop automatic discounting in the three categories where margin fell more than 5 points without unit growth: Urban footwear, Outerwear and Accessories. Together they hold $712M of revenue and 4.2 points of the margin drop, about $101M of result. Start with Outerwear, already running at 61% of units sold on discount with last season's stock still unsold.

scenarios.question: Which products ran out of stock this week?

queries.question: Daily stock by SKU, last 7 days
Estimated lost sales per day out of stock

answer.title: This week's stockouts
answer.lead: Three SKUs were out of stock more than half the week and account for $18.4M in lost sales.

scenarios.recommendation: Restock all three before Friday: they hold 78% of the week's lost sales and all three have stock available in the central warehouse.

nextTurn.question: And if we restock from the central warehouse, how much do we recover?

answer.title: Recoverable by restocking
answer.lead: The stock sitting in the warehouse recovers $14.3M of the $18.4M lost.

scenarios.question: Where did we lose share to generics this season?

queries.question: Sales by region and product line, 24/25 and 25/26 seasons
Average price per litre, ours vs. generic, by distributor

answer.title: Share by region, 25/26 season
answer.lead: We lost 6.4 points in the core region, and 78% of that drop sits in three herbicides.

scenarios.recommendation: Revisit the core region price list before the next distributor order: those three herbicides hold $2,140M of season revenue and every point of share recovered is worth about $67M.

scenarios.question: Where is my margin going this month?

queries.question: Margin by category and discounts approved at the register, last 30 days

answer.title: Margin leak, last 30 days
answer.lead: 71% of the drop sits in two categories, and almost all of it in discounts approved at the counter.

scenarios.recommendation: Cap register discounts on Beverages and Cleaning: that's $4.3M of margin lost this month, and 84% of the cases went over 10% without a supervisor signing off.

scenarios.question: How much capital is sitting still in stock?

queries.question: Valued inventory by SKU and last sale
Restocking vs. sales by category, last 6 months

answer.title: Non-moving stock, February cut
answer.lead: 54% of valued inventory had no sales in the last six months: $128M immobilized.
answer.conclusion: Almost all of the period's growth comes from three categories that kept being restocked at the same rate as the ones that do turn over.

scenarios.recommendation: Start the clearance by stock age with SKUs older than twelve months: that is $71M at cost and 38% of the warehouse.

notChatbot.eyebrow: Why a generic chat is not enough
notChatbot.title: ChatGPT does not solve this, and <accent>it is not only us saying it</accent>
notChatbot.description: Wiring a language model straight into a database is not enough to answer business questions with confidence. Anthropic, the company behind Claude, documented this publicly about its own internal analytics.
notChatbot.statLead: That is how low the accuracy of a model connected raw to a database was at first.
notChatbot.statBody: The difference came from business context layers, clear definitions and constant validation — exactly what Beacon builds before answering your first question.

cards.title: It does not know which number is the right one
cards.description: The same concept — “margin”, “active customer” — lives in several different tables. A generic chat picks one source and answers with the same confidence whether it is right or wrong.

cards.title: It works with stale information
cards.description: Your data and your definitions change all the time. Without a process that keeps them current, the model keeps answering with what it knew months ago.

cards.title: It cannot find what already exists
cards.description: Sometimes the right number is there, but lost among thousands of tables and queries. Without curation, finding it is a needle in a haystack.

notChatbot.source: Source: Anthropic, <link>“How Anthropic enables self-service data analytics with Claude”</link>.

items.question: Is this the same as using ChatGPT or Claude directly?
items.answer: No. Beacon is the layer that securely connects a language model to your real business data, sorts it and trains the agent to answer with your information, not with what the model knows in general.

items.question: What happens to my data during the pilot?
items.answer: Before anything is shared we sign an NDA: it is part of the pilot terms and bars Nivii from sharing your data externally. From there it is loaded into an isolated clean room, exclusive to your company. It is never shared or mixed with other clients' data, and it is deleted at the end of the pilot if you do not move forward.

items.question: Do I need clean, organized data before starting?
items.answer: No. That is precisely the problem we solve. You hand us the data as it is — in spreadsheets, in your ERP, in your point of sale — and Beacon sorts it out.

items.question: Do I need real-time data for this to work?
items.answer: No. Beacon works with whatever refresh frequency you have: daily, weekly or in batches. Most commercial decisions are not made minute by minute, they are made with the best picture available — and that picture is already enough to find where margin is leaking.

items.question: How much does Beacon cost?
items.answer: It is defined in the conversation after the pilot, based on the volume and complexity of your operation. It is a flat monthly fee, well below hiring a full-time data analyst, and with no lock-in contracts.

items.question: Is there any commitment to run the pilot?
items.answer: None. The two meetings are free and imply no commitment to hire.

items.question: How do you guarantee the accuracy of the answers?
items.answer: Beacon works on your already-sorted data, not the open web, and shows its work: what it queried, from which source and with what logic each answer was built. When a number is a benchmark and not your own data, it says so.

items.question: Do you connect to my ERP, point of sale or management system?
items.answer: Yes. Beacon connects to the systems you already use — point of sale, ERP, spreadsheets and more — and works with your data where it lives. Data scattered across several systems is the starting point, not an obstacle.

items.question: Is it a subscription, or is it mine at some point?
items.answer: It is a monthly fee: Beacon runs in Nivii's cloud and you access the answers while you are subscribed, with no lock-in. If your company later needs the agent running in its own cloud, that is the Nivii Enterprise path: a different product, built for another scale of operation.

items.question: Does my data live in Nivii's cloud? How safe is that?
items.answer: Yes, that is the Beacon model: we hand you the simplicity of not running your own infrastructure. In exchange, your data lives in an isolated environment exclusive to your company, encrypted at rest and in transit, and is never mixed with another client's. If you would rather your data never leave your own perimeter, that is the Nivii Enterprise architecture.

items.question: How long until we see value beyond the pilot?
items.answer: The pilot already shows you real answers about your business in under a week. Once the subscription starts there is no months-long curve: Beacon keeps answering on refreshed data and taking on the new questions your team brings.

items.question: Is this like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini?
items.answer: No, and the difference matters. Those are the engine: foundation models built by a handful of companies. Nivii is everything around the engine: the architecture that connects securely to your data, learns your business, checks its own accuracy and returns answers you can trust enough to act on. It is the same reason tools like Cursor or Harvey are valuable without building their own models. And it runs inside your own cloud, on your own data: something a public chatbot cannot do.

items.question: How do you ensure accuracy?
items.answer: Accuracy is engineered in, not assumed. The agent works from governed, cleaned data rather than the open web, validates its own outputs and shows its work: the query, the source and the logic behind every answer. When a number is a benchmark and not your own data, it says so.

items.question: Do you connect to SAP, Salesforce or other systems?
items.answer: Yes. Nivii connects to the systems you already run — SAP, Salesforce, data warehouses, spreadsheets and more — and works with your data where it lives, inside your own cloud. Disconnected sources are the starting point, not a blocker.

items.question: Does our data ever leave our environment?
items.answer: No. Nivii runs inside your own cloud and your data stays within your perimeter. The only outbound call is to the model provider, and even that can be eliminated with in-cloud models like Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Vertex AI or SAP AI Foundry.

items.question: What if our data is not clean?
items.answer: Every company's data is messy: that is our starting point, not a blocker. Dedicated cleaning agents identify your most reliable sources first, so you get trustworthy answers in weeks while data quality keeps improving underneath.

items.question: How long until we see value?
items.answer: About 12 weeks to a live pilot on your real data, and it works roughly 95% like the production system. From there you are in production in your own cloud by month 4, and by month 12 your team runs the agent on its own. The pilot is not a proof of concept: it is the real product, already most of the way there.

items.question: What do we commit to for the pilot?
items.answer: Very little. The pilot runs at cost and on a read-only extract of your data, in Nivii's cloud, so you can prove the value before signing anything. Our rule is simple: no ROI, no contract.

items.question: What does our IT team need to sustain it?
items.answer: During the pilot, nothing beyond the read-only extract. In production the agent runs in your cloud with your own SSO and your access policies; your team trains alongside throughout, so operations stay in-house and do not depend on us.

openPositions.title: Decision Scientist – Data & AI Implementation
aboutNivii: Imagine you are the leader of an area in a large company and it's monday morning. The results from last month have just come in and they are not what we were expecting... maybe margins are down, stock has gone up, talent is leaving faster or our products quality is suffering. What happened is something most companies know how to find, but why and what to do is much much harder and slower. You needed instant answers from deep within your data, but without them you keep using only your intuition.

At Nivii, we're rethinking how people interact with business data. Our conversational AI system lets users ask questions in natural language and receive clear, actionable answers—instantly and visually. By combining large language models, data orchestration, and chart generation into a seamless interface, we help teams move from data to decisions faster than ever before. We haven't built a chatbot or another "talk to your data" — we've built a thinking partner, an evolution of consulting.

Our product is already live, serving real users across LATAM, with early traction from teams that need answers, not dashboards. We're a small, hands-on team based in Buenos Aires, passionate about usability, clarity, and helping people reason better with data.
aboutRole: We're looking for someone to join Nivii's Decision Science team. We are the team that makes sure our agents give back really insightful answers. To do that we usually need to make sure they have clean, reliable inputs, sharp reasoning pathways and the right business context.

This is a hybrid role: part data, part analysis, part AI experimentation. Perfect for someone who loves variety and thrives in early-stage environments but who loves being able to have a material impact in our product and our client's business.
responsibilities: Conduct data analysis: Look at the numbers, find meaningful patterns, and translate them into clear, actionable insights for the business
Iterate on agent development: Adjust prompts, refine reasoning, test improvements, run evaluations, and help our agents answer each day a little better

Design and develop creative internal tools: Build inventive, lightweight utilities and frameworks that push our data analysis forward—whether that's automating investigative workflows, surfacing insights faster, or crafting new ways for the team to interact with data
Help shape the product: Work closely with Engineering on product features and with our Commercial team to understand client needs and tune our AI systems to solve them effectively
Build and maintain data pipelines: Connect sources, model tables, ensure data quality, and keep our agents well-fed with clean, structured information
requirements: Really strong analytical background. Often people in this area have engineering, economist, planning or other data-driven roles
You are a very curious person who self teaches whenever is needed. In the cutting edge of Gen AI we often find that to solve a problem we need to learn new things
You tend to excel at breaking down problems and when you see something we could do better you try to fix it
